what_happened: On job 20261014-184843-jms6, a prompts-related request, the user corrected Athena's accepted reading 1. The reading had made line wrapping in docs a criterion that could block the job. The user said wrapping is only a nit and must not block. So the reading did not match what the user meant.
cause: Readings turn every observed convention or quality concern into an acceptance criterion. Nothing separates outcomes that must hold from cosmetic preferences that should be reported without blocking. Athena has no stated rule that formatting details are non-blocking unless the user says otherwise. Because of this, the over-strict reading was accepted and only the user's correction caught it.
prevention: Add a default to reading drafting: acceptance criteria cover only outcomes the user stated or that the work cannot function without. Cosmetic and style matters (line wrapping, whitespace, wording preferences) are listed as non-blocking notes unless the request explicitly makes them required. The verifier must not reject a job for a non-blocking note.
proposed_request: When drafting a reading, list acceptance criteria only for outcomes the request states or that the work needs in order to function. Put cosmetic or style details, such as line wrapping in docs, in a separate non-blocking notes section unless the request explicitly requires them. The verifier must report these notes but never reject a job because of them. Then redo the reading for job 20261014-184843-jms6 with line wrapping as a non-blocking note.
